Lett. 118, 016602 (2017)) to show that driven-dissipative systems display thermodynamic phase transitions when quasiparticle lifetimes are significantly longer than thermalization times. Our study investigates how dimensionality and interaction strengths influence the thermalization level of optically spun traps and differentiates the imprint of trapping from these other effects. By measuring polariton populations across a square array of pumped probes in nonresonant settings versus those activated by individual sources separately, we demonstrate that trapping and altered density of states cause substantial redistribution of these particles. Notably, we identify remarkably efficient excitonic-ionic scattering beneath condensation thresholds through the loss of inflection-point modes. Ultimately, this work enhances our comprehension of polarization dynamics within interacting particles across differing geometries of optical potentials.

The explosion of parameters in deep learning, driven by a "bigger is better" philosophy, increasingly hinders the practical deployment of state-of-the-art networks in environments with limited computational budgets, renewing the relevance of model compression strategies. However, the standard assessment of compression involves trade-offs primarily derived from high-resource benchmarks. This paper shifting the focus to compression's effects in data-constrained regimes by introducing the "low-resource double bind," a challenging combination of scarce data and limited compute often encountered in low-resource NLP. While thoroughly studied elsewhere, the performance dynamics of this specific setting remain poorly understood. Our study provides novel insights into how model capacity interacts with generalization constraints within data limits for machine translation. Experimental evaluation of magnitude pruning for translations to and from English—specifically covering German and three low-resource languages, Yoruba, Hausa, and German—demonstrated a nuanced impact. Sparsity notably preserves performance on recurring examples but disproportionately degrades accuracy for infrequent sentences. Furthermore, sparsity significantly enhances robustness out of the training distribution, benefiting models when target data distributions vastly differ from training data. Ultimately, our results indicate that reducing parameters inhibits over-memorization of rare data attributes, suggesting that compression offers a vital pathway to resolving the low-resource double bind.

Natural language Processing remains an area dominated by active research and innovation, yet it relies heavily on vast datasets for supervised learning. Such demand persists significantly within applications involving Arabic and its national dialects. Today's Data Science landscape faces scarcity in open-access labeled corpora for this linguistic scope, a deficit that impedes research and innovation. Addressing this limitation, we introduce an open dataset comprising social media content from multiple Arabic dialects. Sourced from the Twitter platform, the collection contains over 50,000 posts across five national dialects and features labels designed to support application areas such as dialect detection, topic identification, and sentiment analysis. We are making this dataset freely available to stimulate further work and innovation in Arabic-NLP and social media studies, alongside a report on various models built using it and their resulting performance metrics.

Monte Carlo rendering techniques are standard in creating photorealistic graphics, yet they demand sampling vast numbers of rays per pixel to achieve accurate global illumination, leading to prohibitive computational costs. Addressing this limitation, we propose a hybrid rendering approach that substantially accelerates Monte Carlo workflows. Our method initially produces two distinct renders: one featuring low resolution but dense sampling (low-resolution/high-sample-rate), and a second utilizing full resolution but sparse sampling (high-resolution/low-sample-rate). A convolutional neural network is then deployed to merge these outputs, simulating the quality of a fully sampled full-resolution render. We frame this fusion as a super-resolution challenge, where LRHS provides a low-resolution input, and a second HRLS render—crucial for capturing high-frequency details that low-sample-rate interpolation cannot retrieve—enhances quality. Experimental results demonstrate that our technique outperforms contemporary Monte Carlo denoising algorithms in speed without compromising fidelity, validated on both the BCR and Gharbi datasets. Handling optimization problems governed by partial differential equations (PDEs) with uncertainties typically requires various discretizations and simplifications, including finite-dimensional representations of spaces, sample-based estimates for risk, smooth substitutions for nonsmooth functions, penalized constraints, and other potential sources of error. This paper investigates the efficacy of solutions derived from approximation-based methods while also deriving optimality gap estimates for general optimization tasks defined on metric spaces. Provided that these modeling discrepancies diminish and certain conditions are met, we prove that limiting controls can achieve optimality gaps as close to zero as desired. The theoretical framework applies broadly to diverse optimization issues featuring multiple expectation, risk, and reliability metrics that depend on PDE states and appear within objective functionals or constraints. Specifically, the study examines cases involving constraints on the probability of buffered failure, modeled via an augmented Lagrangian. We validate this approach using an instance involving elliptic PDEs characterized by random spatially distributed coefficients alongside distributed control variables.

Meeting optimal control standards with fewer sensor requirements is essential for creating cost-effective and computation-efficient controllers in industrial settings. However, conventional machine learning feature selection methods often fail when applied to control domains characterized by dynamic variables where system characteristics can alter over time. We introduce a new approach titled Dual-world embedded Attentive Feature Selection (D-AFS), designed to efficiently identify pertinent sensors for systems undergoing dynamic control. Unlike most standard Deep Reinforcement Learning algorithms that simulate within a single world environment, D-AFS leverages both a physical (real) world and an associated virtual parallel universe containing distorted features and evaluates how Deep Reinforcement Learning responds across both environments to quantify the importance of each feature regarding system control stability. We evaluate its efficiency using an active drag reduction problem on a cylinder in fluid flow, demonstrating that it identifies an optimized layout of just five sensor probes. This setup achieves an 18.7% drag reduction compared to state-of-the-art configurations that utilized 151 probes, and it surpasses five-probes configurations designed by human experts by 49.2%. Furthermore, applying D-AFS across four OpenAI classical control scenarios revealed that it either matches or outperforms the sensor configurations originally provided. Ultimately, our results indicate D-AFS offers a promising pathway toward designing efficient, optimal sensors for use in both industrial applications and research experiments. We have made our open-sourced codes publicly accessible at https://github.com/G-AILab/DAFS.

Although Rao's score tests, akin to classical likelihood ratio tests, have previously avoided multivariate and high-dimensional contexts, they are now proposed as crucial tools for high-dimensional inference to be more widely utilized beyond standard settings. While existing applications for testing correlation matrices within multivariate normal distributions generally focus on fixed dimensions, they lack recognition. In our paper, we examine these fixed-dimension tests and derive their asymptotic behavior to validate them. Building upon foundational concepts from tests on correlations of normally distributed multivariate data, we develop not merely classical versions (Rao's) but Rob variants with robustness guarantees. While involving extensive computations, our derivation results are effective and concise for any arbitrarily fixed dimensions, and further formulas facilitate extension to alternative tests regarding correlation parameters or location/scattering. We conduct high-dimensional simulations across various standard or contaminated normal models, demonstrating performance against likelihood ratios in a variety of contexts; our outcomes indicate the validity of tests and show specific efficiency for the Rao score tests even outside multivariate distributions, and that they perform optimally when models contain outliers.

This paper explores integrated data and energy networks incorporating Device-to-Device (D2D) communication operating within an Integrated Data and D2D (Ded2D) framework. This system facilitates base station transmissions of data and energy to respective Information-Urgent (IUs) and Energy-Urgent (EUs) users using an information and energy transfer (TFIET) approach based on time allocation. Additionally, the system allows D2D communications to share the spectrum alongside base station operations. Consequently, the system addresses expanding energy and spectrum requirements in next-gen networks. Nevertheless, D2D-generated interference and wireless path loss can notably impair data throughput for IUs. To mitigate these challenges, the work proposes deploying Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces (IRS). Subsequently, an optimization problem is constructed to optimize beamformers for both IU data and EU energy delivery, along with TFIET time allocations, D2D transmit powers, and IRS phase shifts. The objective function seeks to maximize the minimum throughput among IUs, subject to EU harvested energy levels and D2D data rate thresholds. Given that the max-min optimization problem is non-decisive without approximation, the authors devise a computationally efficient alternating descent algorithm. Simulation outcomes confirm the validity of the proposed scheme.

Falls rank as a primary contributor to injury deaths among the global elder population, making effective fall detection crucial for mitigating associated injuries and complications. While wearable gadgets and ambient sensors facilitate fall monitoring, they often hinder user compliance or generate false positive alerts in video-based systems. RGB cameras offer a non-contact alternative yet face dual challenges regarding shifting lighting environments and data privacy constraints. Beyond hardware limitations posed by variable conditions and camera positions, developing robust detection algorithms from a machine learning angle is complicated by the erratic nature and scarcity of actual fall events. This paper introduces an unrolling algorithm derived from the iterative subspace optimization method (SOM) to address full-wave inverse scattering problems (ISPs). The resulting architecture, SOM-Net, naturally integrates the Lippmann-Schwinger physical model directly into its network structure. SOM-Net utilizes the deterministic induced current and initial raw permittivity images derived via back-propagation (BP) as inputs. Within successive sub-network blocks corresponding to SOM iterations, the system updates the current and permittivity estimates iteratively. Finally, a complete predicted current solution is generated from the SOM-Net, enabling the analytical deduction of both the scattered field and permittivity image. Model parameters are tuned through supervision based on a total loss function designed to simultaneously ensure the internal consistency of the current, scattered field, and permittivity as dictated by the governing equations. Extensive numerical tests using both simulated and real-world datasets confirm that proposed SOM-Net outperforms conventional approaches on various benchmarks, including challenging cases featuring scatterers with complex profiles or high permittivity, highlighting the framework's strong generalization capabilities. Ultimately, this approach leverages the power of deep network unrolling, constructing a functional conduit between traditional iterative algorithms and modern deep learning techniques for ISP resolution.

We propose an affordable first-principles method for characterizing quantum paraelectricity by integrating density functional theory (DFT) for the electronic system with a quantum mechanical treatment of ions based on solving the single-particle Schr\"odinger equation using the DFT-derived potential. Evaluating the approach with BaTiO$_3$, SrTiO$_3$, and KTaO$_3$ as benchmarks demonstrates that ferroelectric, paraelectric, and quantum paraelectric states can be readily differentiated using simple metrics derived from standard DFT and DFT perturbation theory calculations. Our findings on how isotope substitution (specifically replacing oxygen-16 with oxygen-18) and strain affect quantum paraelectric behavior reveal that while the isotopic change has a surprisingly minimal impact, strain levels within experimental ranges can cause significant alterations. Lastly, we survey various phonon mass assignments found in existing literature and determine their physical relevance by contrasting them with our results that inherently circumvent such a choice by employing mass-weighted coordinates.

Distributed consensus acts as a fundamental pillar for various distributed infrastructures, notably blockchains and distributed databases. The novel protocol Canopus offers a scalable solution where live nodes concur upon an ordered sequence of transactions, distinct from prior methods due to the absence of leader dependency. Instead, Canopus employs a virtual tree overlay for message propagation to curb network congestion on overloaded connections, while utilizing hardware redundancies within racks and network fabrics to minimize protocol complexity and communication costs. These mechanisms empower canpus-managed systems of massive scale without considerable performance loss. Although standard Canopus maintains resilience against node and network faults, its heavy emphasis on speed makes it vulnerable to other failure scenarios, such as a total system freeze following the loss of an entire single rack. furthermore, basic consensus can compromise consistency when subject to Byzantine attacks. To address these limitations, this introduction presents RCANOS ("re-lient") that extends functionality to preserve liveness, ensuring system advancement despite diverse faults, by employing accurate recovery procedures even with unreliable detection methods while resisting Byzantine threats. RCANOS additionally guarantees correctness by ensuring live nodes reach consensus regarding transaction ordering despite the presence of attackers or network fragmentation.

Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) are increasingly used for video analysis on mobile devices to reduce processing delay through integration on dedicated Neural Processing Units (NPUs). However, resource constraints on these NPUs necessitates compressing the DNNs to improve speeds, often compromising classification accuracy. To mitigate this reduction, we introduce a Confidence Based Offloading (CBO) architecture designed for mobile video analytics. The primary challenge lies in selecting the optimal moment to rely on the local NPU's output—based on the inference confidence—or to transmit video frames offload to a cloud server for enhanced precision. We identify flaws in using raw probability scores for this binary decision-making process and propose confidence calibration techniques to optimize performance. Subsequently, we formalize the CBO problem with the dual goal of maximizing accuracy within temporal limits by proposing an adaptive mechanism that identifies whether frames should be offloaded, and at what resolution, contingent on the computed confidence and current network state. Extensive experimental validation demonstrates that this solution significantly surpasses existing methodologies, confirming the substantial performance gains and the scalability of this approach.

We have demonstrated the explicit correspondence between classical soliton gas theories and Generalized Hydrodynamics (GHD), the many-body theory for classical and quantum integrable univers. This connection was realized by deriving a GHD framework specifically for the soliton gas arising in the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation. Specifically, we predict the precise forms for the free-energy density, currents, and static correlation structures of the conserved charges within this soliton gas framework. This relies on characterizing soliton statistics akin to classical particles, with our derived static correlation matrices subsequently validated via numerical simulations. Additionally, we formulate conjectures for time-dependent dynamical correlations by directly adopting GHD findings, thereby opening the pathway to immediate predictions for various non-equilibrium statistical properties such as soliton transport fluctuations, their associated diffusion, and large-deviation characteristics.

People naturally develop intricate internal representations of their surroundings, encompassing the scene's geometry and meaning across varied hierarchical levels—from objects and rooms to entire structures. These human cognitive maps also incorporate static elements, dynamic agents, and the relationships defining their states (e.g., occupancy) over time. However, robots typically possess only disjoint or fragmented views, ranging from sparse geometric primitives to simple object collections. Addressing this divide between human and robotic understanding, this work proposes a "3D Dynamic Scene Graph (DSG)," a unified framework that seamlessly merges metric and semantic information within dynamic settings. The structure consists of nodes depicting spatial concepts at multiple levels of abstraction and edges modeling spatio-temporal interactions between them. Furthermore, we present **Kimera**, the pioneering automated methodology for generating DSGs directly from visual-inertial data by leveraging advanced capabilities in visual-inertial SLAM, metric and semantic 3D reconstruction, object localization, human pose estimation with shape analysis, and scene parsing. Extensive testing across diverse real-world benchmarks and photorealistic simulations—introducing for the first time the **uHuman3** dataset focused on crowded indoor and outdoor scenarios—demonstrates Kimera SOTA performance in visual-inertial SLAM, real-time extraction of precise 3D geometric meshes rich in semantic detail, and rapid construction of complex DSGs (containing numerous humans and objects). Additionally, we showcase the integration of the DSG into a robust real-time hierarchical semantic path-planning framework, and all core algorithms are open source.

Belief Propagation (BP) is a message-passing algorithm employed for approximate inference within Probabilistic Graphical Models (PGMs), albeit with widespread application in domains like computer vision, error-correcting codes, and protein folding hindered by its limited practical convergence and speed on complex tasks. Due to the high parallelizability of BP, leveraging multi-core GPUs could notably enhance its performance, provided that the challenge of scheduling message updates is addressed effectively, as these decisions critically impact system efficiency. This paper examines message scheduling strategies for BP execution on GPUs, revealing a tradeoff where increased parallelism affects the speed-convergence balance and demonstrating that current scheduling methods fail to exploit this tradeoff optimally. Consequently, a new randomized scheduling technique, termed Randomized Belief Propagation (RnBP), is proposed; comparative metrics show that RnBP surpasses existing GPU implementation approaches.

Recently, Bayesian optimization over the latent spaces of deep autoencoder models (DAEs) represents a promising solution for optimizing difficult black-box functions on structured but discrete and complex-to-enumerate domains, such as molecules. By mapping inputs into a continuous latent space, DAEs significantly simplify the terrain of the standard search process, enabling the easier application of established optimization techniques. However, although the latent space simplifies the problem, it often remains high-dimensional, suggesting a mere shift of the structured optimization burden onto a high-dimensional landscape rather than a definitive resolution. Consequently, merely having a suitable latent space is insufficient. We propose LOL-BO, an adaptation of the trust region technique from recent high-dimensional Bayesian literature to fit a structured optimization setting. Instead of keeping the encoder and the surrogate kernel separate, we utilize the encoder to act functionally as both a global DAE component and a localized deep kernel within a trust region, thereby better synchroning local optimization behaviors in both input and latent spaces. Testing on six real-world benchmarks demonstrates an improvement of up to twentyfold over existing latent space methods. This outcome highlights that refining optimization strategies, alongside developing superior deep architectures, remains crucial for advancing these approaches in real-world structured optimization.

Free-space quantum channels, vital for conducting fundamental quantum mechanics tests and enabling quantum technologies in open spaces, have traditionally relied on direct line-of-sight connections. This limitation arises because standard photon-encoding schemes based on polarization or spatial modes cannot handle photons undergoing random scattering. This work introduces an innovative technique to transmit and retrieve the coherence of non-line-of-sight photons scattered through free space, utilizing an imaging and multimode time-bin interferometer alongside an 8x8 single-photon-detector array for detection. Results show that high time-bin visibility ($95\%$) was maintained even across a broad angular distribution of -45° to +45° scattered photons, while individual detector pixels resolved images within ~0.5° of their field-of-view. These capabilities highlight the feasibility of two advanced applications: 1) employing scattered photons for quantum communication via an indirect path that effectively suppresses background noise, and 2) using joint timing and quantum coherence data to boost image contrast and improve performance in laser ranging under bright ambient conditions. We anticipate that this methodology will open fresh pathways for research aimed at applying photon coherence found in scattered signals to future quantum sensing, imaging, and communication systems in free-space.

Radar and cameras stand as mature, durable, and affordable sensors extensively deployed within the perception frameworks of mass-market autonomous driving. Leveraging their complementary capabilities, the outputs—often combining radar "pins" and 2D bounding boxes from vision systems—are typically fused to optimize detection results. Success in radar-camera fusion heavily depends on precise data association; however, this process is hampered by intricate driving environments, the sparse and noisy character of radar data, and spatial ambiguities arising from 2D boxes. While traditional, heuristic association rules are prone to significant performance drops or total failure in edge cases and difficult scenarios, this study adopts a representation learning approach. We utilize this strategy to probe interactions within the feature space and perform global reasoning. Furthermore, to mitigate the limitations imposed by incomplete annotations, we introduce innovative loss functions and a sample mechanism that encourages human-like logical reasoning. Notably, despite training on noisy labels supplied by rule-based algorithms, our method attained a 92.2% F1 Score, surpassing its teacher by 11.6 percent. Additionally, as a data-driven solution, our approach supports continuous refinement through the systematic mining of corner cases.

We address the challenges of multiview 2D/3D rigid registration for interventions using $ POINT^2 $, a Point-Of-Interest Network designed for both tracking and triangulation. The system learns to identify 2D point-to-point correspondence by tracking random points of interest between pre-intervention and intra-intervention imagery, followed by 3D pose re-evaluation using a triangulation component. The architecture of POINT^2 combines these tracker and triangulation mechanisms, allowing for cooperative feature learning and pose estimation via a forward pass that achieves consistent precision. When contrasted with traditional solutions that need iterative optimization or multiple forward passes for reliable 2D/3D matches, our model is computationally faster by producing accurate results in a forward pass alone thanks to the shift-invariant nature of the Point of Interest (PoI) tracker. The shift invariance also ensures robustness when the camera parameter guess or starting point changes. Large-scale evaluations across clinical cone-beam computer tomography (CBCT) cases prove superiority in accuracy and speed metrics of POINT^2 when compared with similar deep learning-based alternatives in addition to sensitivity robustness when it is used alongside the optimized-based state of art solvers as an initial framework. The experimental results further validate its effectiveness as an efficient pose estimator that enhances robustness and speed by ten folds.

We examine an uncomplicated lattice model characterized by local symmetry, constructed from a crossed module of finite groups. The dynamical variables reside on both the links and the faces within a four-dimensional lattice. Specifically, we prioritize the study of the model's dynamics through both analytical methods and Monte Carlo simulations. Special limits reveal that the model converges into recognized topological quantum field theories. A central finding of our work is a proven factorization theorem; this reduces the calculation of local observable correlation functions to computations within known, simpler models. By integrating this theorem with standard Kaśmierczak-Wannier dualities, we formulate a comprehensive conjectural phase diagram, a structure validated by subsequent numerical experiments. Additionally, we detail the topological charges, underlying symmetries, and their breaking mechanisms. The relevant order parameters identified are the standard Polyakov loop and its extended form, referred to here as a Polyakov surface. The latter is distinct in that the factorization theorem does not apply to it yet proves particularly significant according to our data. Numerical evidence indicates that the expectation value of the Polyakov surface can successfully detect all phase transitions.

This study proposes an iterative learning control (ILC) framework designed for continuously operating repetitive systems lacking initial condition resets, accomplished through a "lifted" system representation that captures the impact of initial conditions on system dynamics while projecting dynamics over multiple iterations. The work also introduces an economic cost function and corresponding update law that factor in multi-iteration future performance rather than just the immediate subsequent step. Convergence of both iteration-dependent variations, including changing initial conditions and applied inputs, has been theoretically proven and empirically demonstrated using a simulated servo-positioning system.

Integrating deep neural networks into robotics often faces the critical challenge of missing uncertainty metrics in prediction outputs. Recent attempts to estimate uncertainty for deep object detectors (DNNs) have achieved limited results, hindered primarily by (1) information loss during the Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS) stage, and (2) an inadequate handling of the multitask, many-to-one characteristics inherent to anchor-based object detection. To address these gaps, this paper introduces BayesOD, a framework that reshapes both standard object detector inference and the NMS components through a Bayesian lens. Experimental evaluations across four standard object detection datasets demonstrate that BayesOD generates uncertainty estimates with superior correlation to detection accuracy, resulting in a substantial 9.77%–13.13% improvement over the Minimum Bayesian Gaussian uncertainty error and a 1.63%–5.23% improvement over the Minimum Bayesian categorical uncertainty error. The associated code will be made available at {\url{https://github.com/asharakeh/bayes-od-rc}}.

This paper analyzes a variant of D. Price's model for bibliographic network expansion. In each iterative step, a fixed quantity of citations is assigned stochastically using a weighted mixture of uniform (accidental) distribution rules and preferential attachment (rich-get-richer) principles. Rather than utilizing standard master equation techniques, we formulate and solve the problem via rank-size distributions. Asymptotically, we demonstrate that this mechanism results in a Pareto type II distribution featuring a highly interpretable parameterization. Furthermore, we establish that the Price model's solution, expressed through rank-size distributions, is equivalent to the expected order statistics from an independent Paretian sample. Additionally, we evaluate the bias and mean squared error of three estimators for the model's core parameters using an extensive dataset of academic publications. Our findings reveal a robust fit across the entire distribution range, rather than merely in the power-law tail. Crucially, the empirical results from this repository indicate that real-world citation dynamics exhibit a greater degree of preferential attachment and a reduced component of randomness compared to previous analyses.

Rapid reaction to signs of impending patient decline is a core principle of healthcare, leading to the creation of a patient-safety approach called a Rapid Response System (RRS). Under this system, individuals who satisfy specific pre-set criteria for immediate danger are quickly evaluated and treated with the aim of stopping their condition from worsening or preventing outcomes such as ICU admission, cardiac arrest, or death. Despite widespread adoption, systematic reviews offer little proof that RRUs significantly improve effectiveness. Usually, the triggers used in these systems are straightforward rules defined by experts based on consensus, designed to spot major physiological issues or clinical signs by sight. If predictive patterns can be detected within patient data sooner than the onset of current detection criteria, intervention methods could prove far more successful. Consequently, this paper utilizes machine learning on electronic medical records to predict when patients are at risk of clinical decline. Our AI-powered models demonstrate higher sensitivity and a longer lead time than the traditional rule-based systems currently used in hospitals. These findings need to be validated through field testing, which, if successful, will allow healthcare providers to embed this approach into existing IT infrastructure and deploy model-generated alerts; doing so could prevent catastrophic events or reduce ICU duration, and may avert transfer to an intensive care unit or reduce the stay length for critically ill patients.

Eclipsing systems are critical for analyzing stars and binary populations, especially those with pulsating constituents that yield precise determinations of component properties and offer a complementary approach to identifying pulsation modes, a factor vital for accurate asteroseismology. Space missions dedicated to obtaining high-precision light curves of tens of thousands of stars—primarily to hunt for exoplanets—have inadvertently illuminated variable stars and renewed focus on binary evolution, significantly accelerating progress in detecting eclipsing binaries with periodic components. This review presents recent findings from the study of pulsating eclipsing systems observed by the {\it Kepler} and TESS missions. Our analysis covers diverse configurations, ranging from semi-detected binaries in nearly circular, non-synchronized orbits, non-singular eclipsing binaries featuring chemically distinct stars, "heart-beat" binaries, to detached, eccentric double-lined systems. Despite their varied nature, all systems contain at least one pulsator, spanning unevolved or slightly evolved stars of spectral types B through F, as well as red giants exhibiting solar-like oscillations. Furthermore, several systems manifest complex behaviors including tides, angular momentum exchange, intermittent mass transfer, and magnetic activity. Understanding how these dynamical influences modulate the excited oscillations in binary pulsations opens a new avenue for unraveling pulsation physics.

Current deep learning architectures often lack robustness and fail to generalize effectively when faced with distributional shifts. Despite significant progress in mitigating this issue, there has been no comprehensive investigation into how specific optimizers and their choices impact generalization under out-of-distribution (OOD) conditions. This research evaluates the performance of prevalent first-order optimizers within empirical risk minimization (ERM) and invariant risk minimization (IRM) frameworks when handling distinct categories of distributional shifts. Leveraging DomainBed, WILDS, and the Backgrounds Challenge for image and text classification tasks, we conduct a rigorous analysis across over 20,000 models with extensive hyperparameter tuning, measuring both in-distribution (IID) and OOD classification accuracy. Our results reveal two key insights: contrary to established norms, adapted optimizers like SGD with adaptive moments underperform non-adaptive counterparts such as vanilla SGD or momentum-based variants; additionally, relationships between IID and OOD performance manifest in three distinct patterns across datasets characterized by linear gains, increasing returns, or diminishing returns. We anticipate these conclusions will guide researchers in selecting optimal optimizers and predicting resulting performance trajectories.

Mobile Networks are poised to revolutionize human interactions and facilitate new realms of connected experiences. However, driven by sophisticated service demands and intricate configuration needs, these networks are increasingly intricate. This growing complexity introduces substantial hurdles throughout deployment, operations, and maintenance, which demand a comprehensive cognitive grasp of the Mobile Network. Artificial Intelligence (AI), capable of simulating intelligent computing behavior, has proven highly effective across many fields, highlighting its capacity to analyze Mobile Network states and facilitate smart decision-making. This study initially outlines an AI-empowered mobile network architecture, addressing challenges related to cognitive complexity, managing decisions within high-dimensional action spaces, and adapting autonomously to dynamic system changes. Furthermore, it evaluates potential AI-based resolutions. Ultimately, the paper presents a machine learning method that correlates the Mobile Network's status directly with perceived quality of service, unifying cognition with decision-making strategies. This approach enables operators to make more intelligent choices to secure service quality, and its superiority and efficacy were validated using a real-world dataset covering 31,261 users across 77 stations over a five-day period.

Ground LiDAR-based place recognition is fundamental to global localization and simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) in robotics and autonomous driving systems. Deep learning's ability to extract meaningful features from 3D LiDAR inputs has enhanced place recognition performance, especially regarding robust re-localization and loop-closing detection under highly varying conditions. However, generating descriptors that efficiently capture valid features from point clouds while remaining invariant to environmental changes and viewpoint rotation remains an open problem. This study introduces AttDLNet, an advanced deep learning framework tailored for 3D LiDAR scene reconstruction, which leverages range-derived proxies and an architecture composed of multiple attention layers. This configuration enables the model to prioritize critical long-range context and interdependencies among features. Experimental validation on the KITTI benchmark via ablation studies confirms that the attention mechanisms enhance overall efficacy, significantly accelerating the resolution of identical locations while surpassing established 3D LiDAR methods. Further insights reveal that middle encoder layers consistently yield higher performance, whereas deeper layers offer greater resilience to rotational shifts. Source code can be accessed at https://github.com/Cyboric/AttDLNet.

Life science experiments and clinical studies often employ factorial designs to repeatedly observe subjects, generating multivariate measurements. Finally, we validate our methodology through multiple proof-of-concept scenarios, confirming the approach is immediately executable and offers a path toward improved insights regarding correlated noise in quantum processors.

Wind generation capacity has grown significantly over the past decades, demonstrating its potential contribution to global energy transitions. Given the inherent variability and complexity of modeling wind, accurately quantifying the spatio-temporal variations of wind power and associated uncertainties is crucial for energy planners. While Machine Learning (ML) has become a standard tool for predicting wind speeds and power outputs (current hourly), existing approaches face several key limitations: (i) neglected spatio-temporal correlations in wind data, (ii) an absence of methods to quantify uncertainties in speed predictions and how these propagate to power estimates, and (iii) predictions at less detailed intervals (typically less than hourly). To resolve these gaps, this study introduces a framework capable of reconstructing a spatio-temporals field on a regular grid using irregular wind measurements collected from specific coordinates. By decomposing data into temporally anchored basis functions and spatially distributed coefficients, this study applies Extreme Learning Machines to model the coefficients spatially, thereby enabling hourly forecasting of a continuous field without restrictive distributional assumptions. The methodology was employed to analyze hourly wind power generation for a dense 250 m x 250 m grid using 100-meter tall towers in Switzerland; this creates the first such comprehensive wind power dataset for the region. Combining these estimates with available land suitability maps yielded projections of the technical potential for Swiss wind energy, offering a critical basis for planners aiming to integrate enhanced wind power into future energy systems.

This discussion covers the thermoelectric transport characteristics of semiconductor nanostructures, specifically those involving a quantum dot linked to quantum wires, focusing on electrical conductance, thermal conductance, and Seebeck coefficient as functions of temperature. Building upon established findings for a zero-bias, particle-hole symmetric, and spin-degenerate Anderson model where electrical conductance maps onto a universal quantum dot conductance, we utilize rigorous renormalization group methods to determine universal thermoelectric transport. Supporting numerical renormalization group results are provided to illuminate the underlying physics, while applying these universal coefficients to current experimental data—plotting electrical resistance and Seebeck voltage against $V_{gate} $ across temperatures within the Kondo regime—enables the calculation of full thermoelectric properties and yields simplified analytical fit equations. Future experimental verification remains limited to certain parameters, specifically due to the current unavailability of comprehensive datasets across a wider temperature span.

Images frequently comprise components containing text paired with bounding box coordinates (e.g., text from screen captures extracted via OCR or object-focused images with labels). To address the localization task where a region corresponding to a textual linguistic expression must be identified within such an image featuring these elements and text segments, we propose a fully learnable end-to-end framework. This approach computes an embedding for each detectable element and maps the result directly onto the specific pixel locations defined by the preceding bounding box within the network's feature representation of that image. We demonstrate a noticeable advantage of our solution compared to strategies that either ignore these text components or only rely on them partially in terms of accuracy. We showcase empirical performance using test sets from COCO and a specialized image-based referring expression dataset curated from webpages.

Although the ethical principles underpinning social Virtual Reality (VR) have not been novel topics, the intense discourse surrounding "safety" in the Metaverse has significantly heightened concerns in this domain. For instance, recent data indicated that approximately 50% of women-identifying VR users have encountered at least one incident of virtual sexual assault or harassment. Access to a safe environment is an inalienable human right, applicable equally to both digital and physical contexts. Consequently, this paper aims to examine the rift between user anxieties regarding safety and the actual design implementations intended to protect users in social VR ecosystems. We begin by systematically analyzing safety concerns through Twitter data and subsequently synthesize the protective measures already adopted across four major social VR platforms. Ultimately, we propose that both future developments in research shifts and platform architectures should incorporate a core attribute known as "boundaries-aware" in the conceptual design.

High-quality training for Neural Machine Translation (NMT) depends heavily on parallel data, yet many language pairs lack sufficient direct corpora. In the absence of direct data, using a single intermediate or pivot language offers a viable alternative by chaining translations from a source-pivot and pivot-target pair. However, this indirect approach compromises quality compared to direct translation on ample data, an effect that worsens in real-time simultaneous translation where the system operates under severe constraint to generate output as source text arrives word-by-word. Addressing these challenges through a novel "multi-pivot" framework within the real-time setting, we develop a method that concurrently translates a single source into multiple pivot languages and simultaneously coerces the multiple outputs into target language using a machine translation multi-source network. Experiments in a low-resource context utilizing Arabic-to-English translation on N-way parallel UN data with French and Spanish pivot sources demonstrate that simultaneously employing these two pivot languages enhances translation performance by as much as 5.8 BLEU points.

Aditya-L1 represents the Indian Space Research Organization's (ISRO) maiden solar telescope launched into space. The setup features four remote sensing payloads—including a coronagraph for visible and infrared data, a NUV full-disk camera, and soft X-ray plus hard X-ray spectrometers covering the entire solar disk—as well as three instruments for in-sita analysis, among which is a magnetometer. Specifically built to capture magnetic field fluctuations during high-energy events, Aditya-L1 pioneers a multi-channel space-based approach for solar study, delivering extensive coverage from X-rays through infrared spectra while recording local magnetic field conditions at L1.

This research outlines the advantages and challenges associated with a robot bartender equipped with the capability to adjust interactions based on individual user preferences regarding hobbies, beverages, and music. While we posit that personalization enhances human-robot engagement and that leveraging user data improves the interaction, this reliance raises issues of privacy sharing. Consequently, we propose an evaluation method to examine people's perspectives and their privacy concerns in the context of interacting with such robots. Through a within-subject experiment, we compared participants' experiences when interacting initially with an informed-less robot, followed by a session where the robot understood their preferences. Results indicate that fewer than 60% of participants were indifferent to providing personal details to the robot, suggesting significant concern among them about information sharing.

Deep learning networks have long proven to be vulnerable to deliberately engineered adversarial examples. Previous research has focused heavily on query-optimisation attacks—whether against white-box or black-box models—and the corresponding defenses against them. This work, by contrast, shifts focus to the overlooked realm of Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) vulnerabilities. Adopting an MitM stance effectively neutralizes traditional attack vectors: first because acquiring model outputs via multiple queries is impractical in this scenario; second because single-use attacks cannot be easily generalized across new data, thereby lowering attacker efficiency. To counter these limitations, we explore crafting adversarial examples dynamically (on-the-fly). While this approach offers potential via generative models such as Variational Auto-Encoders (VAAE), their adversarial capabilities remain underexploited specifically from an MitM perspective. We investigate structures of ribbon and ladder polymers situated in poor solvent environments. Link prediction in signed graphs is a crucial task with broad applicability across multiple domains, formulated as a binary classification problem that determines whether the connection between any two nodes is positive or negative. Significantly, SigGAN integrates requirements such as information from negative edges, addresses the high class imbalance between positive and negative edges, and incorporates Structural Balance Theory. Experimental evaluations on several real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate that our proposal surpasses current state-of-the-art methodologies, confirming its effectiveness.

Visual place recognition (VPR) focuses on identifying a location from photographs that has been encountered before. Numerous studies have proposed enhancements  for VPR algorithms, particularly a recently popular technique called multi-process fusion. This approach involves running various VPR systems concurrently and aggregating their results to improve overall accuracy. However, a significant gap exists: there is currently no clear methodology for selecting the right methods from hundreds of options and combining them effectively for superior performance. To address this, the present paper systematically analyzes, for the first time, the complementarity among leading VPR techniques, aiming to discover combinations that enhance effectiveness. This framework calculates both upper and lower limits for synergy and predicts the highest achievable VPR performance. Finally, experiments evaluating eight advanced VPR approaches across ten common datasets demonstrate significant potential when these methods are combined optimally.

Medical imaging collections typically face domain shift stemming from scanner vendor differences and varying protocols, thereby raising doubts regarding the generalization capabilities of machine learning models. A common contemporary approach involves model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML) for DG, which leverages past training to accelerate adaptation to new evaluation tasks; however, clinical environments often provide only a small number of labeled source domains. This scarcity restricts the creation of training instances and increases the likelihood of overfitting to specific tasks within the standard paradigm. This paper introduces a novel DG framework for medical image classification featuring episodic training with enhanced task augmentation. Grounded in meta-learning principles, our methodology constructs knowledge transfer from simulated episodic tasks to genuine clinical test scenarios via DG. Addressing the real-world limitation of few available source domains specifically leads to our focus on mitigating task-level overfitting through task augmentation to boost diversity during training generation. Furthermore, by leveraging the proposed framework, we utilize a distinct meta-objective designed to normalize deep embeddings of training data. Finally, experiments were conducted on both histological and abdominal CT datasets to verify the proposed method's effectiveness.

Research into social forensics has generated substantial interest in multimodal fake news detection (FND), with existing methods primarily focusing on specialized attention mechanisms to fuse unimodal characteristics. Despite this, critical aspects—namely, how feature similarity should be computed and its specific influence on decision-making in FND, along with the untapped potential of pretrained multi-modal learning models—remain unresolved. To address this, this paper introduces FND-CLIP, a framework for detecting multimodal fake news leveraging Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining (CLIP). The approach begins by extracting deep visual representations from ResNet- and CLIP-based encoders, alongside linguistic embeddings from text using BERT- and CLIP-based encoders. These features are combined by concatenating the CLIP-derived outputs weighted based on measured cross-modal similarity, followed by a process designed to reduce feature redundancy. A dedicated attention mechanism then adaptively aggregates these processed features before they reach the final classifier. Extensive testing on standard fake news datasets demonstrates that the proposed framework excels at mining critical indicators. Notably, FND-CLIP significantly outperforms prior state-of-the-art methods, yielding overall accuracy improvements on Weibo and Politicot and GossipCop by 6.8%, 7.1%, respectively. Furthermore, our results validate that models leveraging CLIP-based pretraining offer enhanced flexibility in selecting effective multimodal features for this domain.

Open-world compositional zero-shot learning (OW-CZSL) aims to identify the conjunction of object states from images, relying solely on a trained subset of individual components and without prior knowledge of unseen object-state pairings. In this framework, the model must navigate a massive search space of all potential compositions, unlike previous approaches that learned joint composition embeddings. Instead, this work returns to a basic CZSL strategy where object states are predicted by classifying state and object features independently rather than together. By endowing both state and object classifiers with distinct non-linear feature extractors, the method encourages the learning of primitive-specific representations. To refine the search process, the feasibility of compositions is estimated via external knowledge, which prunes the candidate outputs by eliminating impossible pairings. Additionally, a novel scenario termed compositional zero-shot learning with partial supervision (pCZSL) is introduced: in this setup, state labels are available during the first phase while only object labels are available in subsequent stages. The method simultaneously estimates missing states for classifying labels in this incomplete supervision scenario using its derived priors. The Knowledge-Guided Simple Primitives (KG-SP) framework attains state-of-the-art performance in both OW-CZSL and pCZSL, outperforming nearly all contemporary methodologies, a superiority observed even when integrated with semi-supervised learning. This study presents an integer programming framework to integrate deceased donor-initiated chains within paired exchange registries and the general dead-donation waitlist. It explicitly accounts for patients registered on both systems. Hybrid Question Answering (HQA) involves answering queries by utilizing heterogeneous data sources, such as passages linked to specific table cells. As systems become increasingly complex and attacks more advanced, the critical need for autonomous cybersecurity in cyber and cyber-physical systems (CPSs) has intensified. However, many current frameworks depend on static models built on impractical premises or fall short of ensuring essential security and safety requirements. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a novel hybrid autonomous agent architecture designed to optimize reinforcement learning (RL) defense strategies by integrating constraint verification through Satisfiability Modulo Theories (SMT) directly into the agent's decision-making loop. By embedding SMT verification, the proposed method not only guarantees adherence to security and safety policies but also continuously guides the reinforcement learning process toward producing both safe and optimal decisions—a vital feature for the risky environment of high-consequence CPSs. Experimental evaluation within a simulated CPS setting demonstrates that agents utilizing this architecture rapidly converge on optimal policies and successfully counter a diverse range of attack techniques in 99% of instances.

The problem of identifying the maximum independent set holds central significance in graph algorithm research, particularly within studies on worst-case exact algorithms for NP-hard challenges. In the constrained weighted variant, each node is assigned a specific weight value, with the objective of discovering an independent set that yields the highest aggregate vertex weight. This research introduces multiple reduction rules coupled with a high-performance exact solution tailored for the maximum weighted independent set problem, utilizing the measure-and-conquer approach to evaluate the time complexity bound. Applicable to general weighted graphs, the proposed method demonstrates particularly efficient runtime performance on sparse graphs. It successfully improves upon previous time complexity limits established by the measure-and-conquer approach for cubic graphs when restricted to polynomial memory usage, achieve a runtime of $O^*(1.1443^n)$ for cases where the average vertex count is three, an advancement that supports usage alongside only polynomial space.

Global contact tracing has become a cornerstone strategy for curbing the spread of COVID-19. Leveraging digital technologies, specifically smartphones and wearables, authorities can swiftly identify individuals exposed to the virus. To facilitate this, numerous mobile applications have been introduced; yet, mounting apprehensions exist regarding their operational mechanisms and effectiveness. While prior literature offers exploratory insights into public reception by examining diverse sources like news reports and user feedback, no existing solution automatically processes user reviews to extract sentiments to the best of our knowledge. Consequently, we introduce a methodology that transitions from crowd-sourcing for manual annotations to the creation and training of AI models designed for automatic sentiment detection on application reviews. Utilizing eight distinct methods, we achieved an average F1-Score of 94.8%, validating the viability of this automated sentiment analysis. Additionally, we detail prominent strengths, limitations, and user apprehensions associated with these apps. Notably, we have gathered and annotated a large-scale corpus of 34,534 manually tagged reviews from contact tracing implementations spanning 46 different countries. The findings from our analysis and the contribution this proprietary dataset present aim to establish a foundational benchmark for future inquiry within this field.

Gas cycling within the circumgalactic realms of galaxies is established as occurring across multiple phases. The MUSE-ALMA Haloes project assembles an extensive multi-wavelength dataset, featuring both absorption and emission observations aimed at greatly improving our knowledge of the physical characteristics of this circumgalactic medium (CGM). Central to the effort is a concerted observatory initiative utilizing VLT/MUSE, ALMA, and HST. The survey's absorber-focused selection consists of 19 VLT/MUSE interferometric field quasar lines-of-sight, containing 32 strong absorbers with $z_{\rm abs} \le 0.85$ and neutral hydrogen column densities $N_{\rm HI} \gtrsim 10^{18}$ $\rm{cm^{-2}}$ derived from UV spectroscopy. Complementing this, a dedicated HST program spanning 40 orbits delivers UVIS and H-ALPHA/FIR imaging across three bands to map stellar populations, though the primary focus of this paper extends to the galaxy-selected subset. In the combined fields, we identified thousands of candidates (703 redshift-mature ones among nearly 7,000), alongside secure millimeter observations via ALMA to examine molecular content. Here we outline comprehensive science goals targeting selection methodology; observational strategy, processing protocols; identification procedures. Additionally, extensive catalogs are released revealing spectral photometry across all VLT/MUSE, ALMA, and HST bands, matched to redshift constraints. Syncretizing these data streams facilitates simultaneous profiling of stars, atomic gas, and molecules—encompassing a robust census of condensed baryons within complex cosmic environments.

Given the anticipated rise in frequency and intensity of wildfire events, developing enhanced prediction models is essential for risk mitigation and resource optimization. By leveraging remote sensing data, researchers can construct valuable spatiotemporal statistics to inform management practices. This paper proposes a dynamic model, utilizing a deep neural network trained on historical burned acreage and climate information to forecast wildfire risks across five specific regions in western North America. The model incorporates unique capabilities designed for robust prediction assessment, specifically dynamic online estimation and time-series analysis, while accounting for localized triggers and confounding factors that arise from data uncertainties when state conditions are only partially observed for specific geographic isolation between fire sites or may introduce correlations. In comparison to existing methods, our framework—which effectively addresses the limitations of incomplete observational states within time-segments—achieved average improvements in predictive performance.

This study addresses the integration of Energy-based Models (EBMs) to guide motion optimization. Being neural networks that represent expressive probability density distributions as parameterized Gibbs energies, EBMs offer an implicit framework ideal for use as optimization factors or initial sampling distributions. Consequently, they serve as potent candidates for embedding data-driven priors into motion optimization tasks. This work details the specific modeling and algorithmic strategies necessary to adapt EBMs for such applications. Furthermore, we examine the advantages of adding extra regularizers during EBM training when utilizing gradient-based optimizers and introduce several architectures designed to learn generalizable distributions for manipulation tasks. Finally, we demonstrate multiple scenarios for integrating these priors into motion optimization and assess their effectiveness across real robot experiments and simulations based on learned EBNs.

This study investigates control issues for fractional, non-instantaneous, and impulsive functional evolution equations featuring state-dependent delays, characterized by Caputo fractional derivatives within Banach spaces. The primary aim is to establish adequate conditions guaranteeing the approximate controllability of such systems in separable, reflexive Banach environments. Utilizing both the resolvent operator method and Schauder's fixed point theorem in our derivations, we achieve the desired objective with particular attention to the approximate controllability of linear systems—an area underrepresented in current literature. Furthermore, we present a concrete example demonstrating the practical efficacy of our findings. Additionally, we identify limitations in existing research concerning the characterization of mild solutions and phase spaces alongside the study of approximate controllability for fractional impulsive system dynamics in Banach contexts.

The enumeration of Steiner trees is an established theoretical issue for which many complexity analyses and algorithms exist, yet practical methods remain nonexistent. This work addresses the Steiner tree enumeration problem specifically from a practical standpoint. We introduce a "Problem Cost Constrained Minimum Spanner" definition, seeking the enumeration of minimum Steiner Trees whose weights are bounded by a specified limit. Our approach centers around a binary decision-diagram-based algorithm designed to solve the task, using these diagrams to effectively compact and display the entire range of minimum Steiner Trees. These structures are then explored, with a focus pruning out any Steiner Trees that surpass the established weight limits. Our algorithm construction is enhanced via an innovative technique to build BDDs and has been proven to optimize resource allocation by controlling memory and computing expenses while limiting the output. This process is scalable, offering a partial subset instead of full minimum Steiner Trees. Our algorithm demonstrates a robust and efficient performance when implementing real tests, easily exceeding the current methods' ability on real-world networks.

Accurately setting sales prices is critical for companies; consequently, forecasting time series pricing data is significant from both an economic and data science standpoint. This study evaluates various techniques for predicting sales prices used by an Italian distributor of food, aimed at moving traditional manual pricing tasks into automation. We analyze ARIMA models—and establish their efficacy in economic contexts as benchmarks—against Facebook's easy-to-deploy Prophet tool and long short-term memory deep learning methods, including convolutional and long short-term memory recurrent networks using CNN. Findings from analyzing a long series suggest that, overall, Prophet and ARMA yield similar predictions; ARMA performs adequately for the task, while LSTM is quite effective, suggesting that convolution network combination is most efficient for the task.

Image restoration and image segmentation are two pivotal areas in image processing that have already seen substantial progress. This study introduces a novel multi-stage segmentation framework designed by integrating restoration techniques into segmentation processes. By incorporating the capabilities inherent to restoration tasks, our model achieves robust segmentation performance on challenging inputs such as high-noise images, blurry scenes, data with corrupted pixels, and multi-valued image datasets. Specifically, we demonstrate the adaptability of the piecewise constant Mumford-Shah segmentation scheme; through a simple extension, it can handle noise, blur, or missing data in both grayscale and multi-valued images once a new data-fidelity term derived from restoration theory is introduced. We further present a solving method based on an alternating algorithm with three variables that converges efficiently under relaxed stability assumptions. Empirical evaluations across various real and synthetic datasets show that our approach consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, exhibiting particular strength when processing blurred images and those containing missing information values.

Although reinforcement learning (RL) theoretically enables robots to autonomously adjust to new tasks, current implementations demand excessive trials. To facilitate rapid adaptation to new tasks via a meta-learning framework—focusing particularly on industrial insertions—we address this issue in this paper. Rapid learning is essential because numerous robot trials pose significant risk to hardware, yet adaptation is promising given the substantial overlap of learnable experience across different insertion applications specificities within this domain. Our approach overcomes two specific hurdles associated with applying meta-learning: first, standard on-demand RL meta-learning requires lengthy meta-evangelical training processes; conversely, we introduce a reduced-volume meta-RL technique using exclusively retrospective data, thereby bypassing complex off-site operations and achieving instant performance updates using simple meta-RL. Additionally, conventional meta-RL often falters when faced with novel tasks that deviate significantly from prior datasets, necessitating precise control in the industrial sector where success ratios matter immensely. To address this dual challenge, we combine context-dependence meta-learning with straightforward post-habitual refinements: when encountered themes align with previous datasets, context-driven evolution allows instantaneous adaptation; otherwise, gradual refinement is attempted. Our method demonstrates exceptional convergence for a diverse set of insertions without expensive training attempts initially required for initial skill acquisition. Video demonstrations are accessible at https://sites.google.com/view/offline-metarl-insertion.

This study examines deterministic SIS dynamics on extensive networks originating from a minimal set of infected nodes. By employing relaxed conditions, our results demonstrate that any two resulting epidemics on identical networks operating with the same parameters are effectively congruent, up to a time shift, provided the initial conditions remain sufficiently scarce, even if the initial infection distributions differ. The theoretical boundary conditions for the scenario starting infinitely far in the past are established as a nontrivial eternal solution that bridges both epidemic-free states: those where there is no active transmission versus the regime established under equilibrium. The proposed analysis applies to several widely used theoretical frameworks, specifically the N-Intertwined Mean-Field Approximation and the Inhomogeneous Mean-Field Approximation.

Although numerous research domains acknowledge the significance of learning graphons—and have seen notable advancements specifically regarding denser regimes—contemporary methodologies often stumble in the more difficult scenarios where graph topology exhibits locally uniform distribution due to a dependence on diverging degrees for efficient operation. Addressing this, the proposed study puts forth a robust algorithm capable of operating within the constant expected degree framework, achieving successful rank-$k$ estimates in the $L_2$ distance under a specific generalized spectral condition on graphon eigenvalues, provided the convergence behavior of the first $k$ such eigenvalue satisfies this threshold.

Gamma-Ray Bursts (GRBs) serve as a probe for studying the universe at high redshift levels. Specifically, the Amati relation, which links the isotropic equivalent energy radiance($E_{iso})$ to the spectral peak energy in the burst frame$(E_{p})$ within non-parametric frameworks, allows GRBs to function as distance indicators. This study aims to circumvent low-redshift circularity issues by employing independent Hubble parameter estimates derived from galaxy age-differentials, offering an alternative model-free method for examining these correlations. Applying Gaussian Process modeling on observational data without imposing cosmological assumptions, our research reconstructs luminosity estimates required for $E_{iso}$. 
The resulting Amati relation parameter estimates closely resemble established findings from prior literature.

This study presents the initial measurements of J/$\psi$ production at extremely low transverse momentum ($p_{T}$ < 0.2 GeV/c) in hadronic Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm{NN}}} =$ 200 GeV and U+U collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm{NN}}} =$ 193 GeV. Intriguingly, at $p_{T}$ < 0.05 GeV/c within the 60–80$\%$ centrality range, the inferred J/$\psi$ nuclear modification factor approaches 52 for U+U collisions and approximately 24 for Au+U collisions at mid-rapidity. This significant enhancement cannot be attributed solely to hadronic processes combined with standard cold or hot medium modifications. The paper also reports, for the first time, experimental data regarding the $dN/dt$ distribution for these very low $p_{T}$ J/$\psi$ mesons; this distribution aligns with expectations from single nuclear targets and indicates potential quantum interference effects. Theoretical comparisons with coherent production models suggest that the enhanced yield results from these mechanisms with a partial loss of coherence due to violent hadronic collisions characteristic of semi-central heavy-ion events. Consequently, existing models strongly indicate that the extraordinary enhancement in the extremely low $p_T$ region arises from coherent photon-nucleus scattering, particularly offering J/$\psi$ mesons produced this way as a potential new tool for quark-gluon plasma investigations.

We offer a qualitative evaluation of potentially problematic outputs from contextualized embedding methods used to identify historical semantic shifts. We introduce an ensemble technique, which surpasses prior contextualized strategies, serving as the foundation for a deep dive into predicted levels of semantic change for English vocabulary across fifty years. Results indicate that these contextualized methods frequently generate high change scores even when no actual diachronic semantic shift occurs, a phenomenon with at least some degree of uncertainty regarding its validity. We explore these complex instances extensively, using specific examples and offering a linguistic framework for them. Ultimately, we conclude that the distribution-based nature of pre-trained contextualized language models tends to confuse changes in specific lexicographic meanings with genuine variance in contextual variation—an issue that differs from that found in static embedding methods—while often conflating syntactic characteristics with semantic features. Finally, we outline various potential future remedies to address these shortcomings.

Aerial manipulants face unique difficulties due to their highly coupled and non-linear dynamics, as the underlying UAV and its attached robotic arm interact bidirectionally. This mathematical characterization is foundational for many approaches in non-linear control and deep reinforcement learning. Conventional methods fall into two camps: the Lagrangian framework using Euler angles, which introduces singularities, and the Newton-Euler method utilizing quaternions, which imposes algorithmic complexity on calculations. This research introduces a hybrid model that merges the best attributes of both paradigms. By applying quaternion-based parameterization within a Lagrangian framework, the approach achieves a singularity-free representation while retaining Lagrangian simplicity. This work derives the process through detailed analyses of general aerial manipulator kinematic modeling and dynamic formulation. The resulting model has two primary real-world demonstrations: (1) an experimental validation comparison against a real-time physics engine, and (2) a practical application utilizing a calculated-torque feedback linearization controller to assess real-time computational performance as model complexity scales.
This paper examines and proves novel strong convergence theorems for partial sums and Fejér averages in the context of the Vilenkin system.

Probabilistic frameworks for collaborative AI necessitate user modeling, yet state-of-the-art cognitive simulators incur prohibitive computational expenses suitable only offline. We propose widely applicable differentiable surrogate techniques that circumvent these bottleneck, granting access to modern behavior models for real-time use while achieving an effective computational cost that remains unchanged by—and independent of—the original models. Empirical results verify that these surrogables reach comparable performance to likelihood-free inference streams to achieve an eight-orders-of-magnitude faster processing. We demonstrate a real-world application of these models for AI assistant systems within the context of the task for menu-search, previously studied but shown to now be technically viable computationally when employing modern behavior modeling and real-time speedups through these surrogate techniques.

This article outlines the capabilities of Ftklipse, an extendable framework for computer forensics, and serves as a comprehensive specification guide for the project's developers. Operating as a robust thick-client application for forensic investigations, Ftklipse is designed to enable evidence collection, preservation, and analysis. It streamlines investigations by incorporating tools that manage chain of custody and enforce access control policies, along with the ability to perform batch operations. This work introduces a uniform microscopic description for superconductivity in strongly correlated electronic frameworks utilizing the extended $t$-$J$-$V$ model, which incorporates intersite Coulomb repulsion alongside electron-phonon coupling. For the projected (Hubbard) operators, the study formulates and addresses the precise Dyson equations for both normal and anomalous (pair-state) propagants. Employing a self-consistent Born approach to the self-energy within this framework yields a d-wave pairing mechanism characterized by a notably high critical temperature ($T_c$). This pairing arises predominantly from the robust kinematical interaction, comparable to the electronic kinetic energy $t$ with respect to spin fluctuations, far exceeding the exchange interaction strength of $J$. Meanwhile, contributions from the Coulomb and electron-phonon terms to the d-wave pairing are shown to remain negligible. Collectively, these outcomes validate the spin-fluctuation paradigm for room-approaching high-temperature superconductor behavior in cuprates, a theory first advanced in prior phenomenological models.

While sectional-hyperbolic attracting sets for any $C^2$ flow on a compact, finite-dimensional manifold are established to possess only finitely many ergodic physical invariant probability measures, our primary focus is establishing an upper bound on the count of distinct ergodic physical measures within a connected, singular-hyperbolic attracting set of a 3-flow. A crucial characteristic of said bound is its dependence exclusively on the quantity of Lorenz-like equilibria situated in the set. Additionally, concrete examples of singular-hyperbolic attracting sets are presented to demonstrate the optimality (sharpeness) of this limit.

Creating intelligent neuromorphic systems is still difficult; it demands a firm grasp of the core architectural components alongside user-friendly, accessible prototyping tools to expedite the design workflow. We introduce an open-source Loihi emulator built upon the Brian neural network framework, designed to integrate seamlessly with current simulation environments. Our work validates lossless software simulation for discrete spike events and recurrent spiking networks. Additionally, on-chip learning mechanisms are described and implemented, accounting only for minor variances attributed to stochastic rounding. This project offers a unified overview of Loihi's computational architecture and presents a novel, user-convenient Loibi prototyping toolkit intended to simplify the conceptualization and deployment of novel algorithms.
